title: Infineon and Megmeet advance 800 VDC power for AI data centers
html:
Infineon Technologies has teamed up with Shenzhen Megmeet Electrical to develop 800 VDC power architectures for next-generation AI data centers. The collaboration will see Megmeet integrate Infineon’s CoolSiC MOSFET G2 technology into its three-phase AI power shelf to improve energy efficiency, power density and reliability.

The partnership highlights the growing shift toward higher-voltage power distribution as AI workloads push data center power requirements to new levels. For power electronics designers and data center infrastructure suppliers, the move offers insight into how silicon carbide (SiC) technology can help address rising energy demands and increasingly challenging power delivery requirements.

SiC technology boosts AI power efficiency

At the heart of the collaboration is Megmeet’s three-phase power shelf, which uses Infineon’s second-generation CoolSiC MOSFETs to reduce switching and conduction losses.

According to Megmeet, the platform delivers system efficiency well above the peak efficiency requirements of the 80 PLUS Ruby certification, targeting the demanding operating conditions of AI server infrastructure.

The CoolSiC G2 devices also incorporate Infineon’s .XT interconnection technology, designed to reduce thermal resistance and improve heat dissipation. This helps boost reliability and long-term stability while supporting the rapidly changing dynamic loads associated with AI processors.

“As AI server power demands continue to increase, customers are placing ever-higher demands on the efficiency, reliability and scalability of power systems,” said William Zhang, Corporate EVP, General Manager of the Power Solution Business Group at Megmeet.

“By combining Infineon’s leading silicon carbide technology with Megmeet’s deep expertise in digital power, we have successfully developed an industry-leading three-phase power shelf for AI that delivers system efficiency well above the peak efficiency requirements of 80 PLUS® Ruby. Together with Infineon, we are advancing 800 VDC power architectures and next-generation AI data center power infrastructure.”

Expanding 800 VDC power architectures

Beyond the three-phase power shelf, the companies will collaborate on server power supply units (PSUs), intermediate bus converters (IBCs) and solid-state transformers (SSTs).

These technologies are key building blocks for emerging 800 VDC distribution systems, which aim to support higher power densities and more efficient electricity delivery across AI data centers.

The agreement builds on an existing relationship between the companies. Megmeet previously adopted Infineon’s CoolMOS 8 Superjunction MOSFETs and OptiMOS 6 MOSFETs for its single-phase AI server power supply platforms.

The partners now plan to extend their work across next-generation power infrastructure, from server-level conversion to broader data center distribution systems.

For Infineon, the collaboration also strengthens the role of its SiC portfolio in AI infrastructure, as data center operators look for ways to manage increasing power consumption without sacrificing performance or reliability.
